fact: The IEG review says the Public Administration Modernization Project, approved April 2018, included creating a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI); the e-ID subcomponent was removed at the 2022 restructuring, and the PKI's fate is not stated.
Djibouti's president officially launched the Mobile ID platform on 9 February 2026, whose authentication combines the national ID card number and a digital fingerprint, per Digital Business Africa.
Digital Business Africa reports Mobile ID launched in Djibouti with three functions: payment authorisation, authentication and electronic signature.

La Nation reports the Interior Ministry launched the Mobile ID project with TO7 Network, giving citizens a secure digital identifier and an electronic certificate, led jointly by the National Cybersecurity Authority and the population directorate, with pilot phases planned before wide rollout.
